credential_value.algorithm: Set lowerLine = lib.toLower line, remove the first # comment suffix deterministically with builtins.split, then prepend one literal space to produce paddedContentLine. Fail when builtins.match regex paddedContentLine is non-null. The explicit preceding non-[a-z0-9_] boundary and required separator prevent larger-identifier matches; the required non-space/non-# value prevents empty/comment-only values.

executable_command.algorithm: fail when builtins.match regex line is non-null; builtins.match is whole-line, so the trailing .* is deliberate

non_loopback_url_or_host.algorithm: Set lowerLine = lib.toLower line. Use builtins.split url_candidate_split_regex lowerLine, retain only captured URL candidates deterministically, and split each candidate after the scheme at authority_split_regex; every authority must whole-match allowed_authority_regex. A line with one allowed and one forbidden URL fails. Separately use builtins.split bare_candidate_split_regex lowerLine, filter empty fragments, retain tokens whole-matching bare_candidate_regex or bare_ipv6_regex, and reject every retained token except allowed_bare_candidates. Bracketed IPv6 literals and unbracketed concrete IPv6 addresses containing at least two colons are recognized; only ::1 and [::1] are allowed, with a decimal port allowed only in bracketed authority or endpoint syntax. Ordinary undotted prose is never a candidate, Markdown punctuation is a split delimiter, and objectStorage.createLocally is accepted only by its exact lowercased token.

deployment_boundary.fixture_evidence: deployment-boundary names every listed fixture result internally; the canonical positive contains all six exact manifest marker/statement pairs, loopback URLs with and without decimal ports/paths, bracketed and unbracketed loopback IPv6 forms, objectStorage.createLocally, harmless larger credential/Host identifiers, and the byte-exact SigV4 exception. Nested fixture results never add top-level PASS/FAIL/SKIP entries.
deployment_boundary.marker_rule: Each literal marker `<!-- task13:<id> -->` occurs exactly once and is immediately followed by its exact normative statement on the next line.
deployment_boundary.matching_semantics: All predicates are implementable in tests/nix/module-eval.nix without a helper: builtins.match is whole-string POSIX ERE matching only; no PCRE-only lookaround, backreference, inline flag, or word/digit/whitespace shorthand escape is permitted. For case-insensitive checks compute lowerLine = lib.toLower line first. Token boundaries are explicit ASCII classes or deterministic builtins.split token lists with empty/capture fragments removed.
deployment_boundary.positive_host_exception: The byte-exact sigv4-host normative statement above is the only allowed action-before-host line. Mentioning Podman in required local-development prose is allowed, but shell command guidance is not.
required_markers: local-podman-compose
Rootless Podman Compose is local-development-only and MUST NOT be used for production deployment.
native-nixos-systemd
Native NixOS systemd is the sole production deployment path for this repository.
native-minio
Optional native MinIO co-deployment is controlled only by objectStorage.createLocally.
migration-policy
Migrations default to manual; api-prestart is the only optional automated mode.
homelab-ownership
Homelab owns PostgreSQL, Redis, Podman, host, domain, volumes, ingress, secrets, monitoring, backup, and restore.
sigv4-host
MUST NOT unconditionally set, rewrite, or override the MinIO/S3 Host header; SigV4 requires preserving the caller's signed Host value.

final_tree_record_protocol.atomic_reservation_rule: Before delegation/build, helper uses descriptor-keyed same-filesystem mkdir as the sole portable exclusive primitive. It provides process/concurrency/interruption-safe atomic reservation only; no fsync, directory durability, crash/power-loss persistence, atomic-rename durability, or capability preflight is claimed. Only the mkdir holder may invoke once. Concurrent loser or an existing reservation directory after interruption is a zero-action hard blocker; no TTL, reclaim, delete, overwrite, or automatic retry.
final_tree_record_protocol.call_kind_rule: Only exact JSON token call_kind=first is valid for the initial receipt, and only exact JSON token call_kind=fv07_replay is valid for the sole FV07 replay receipt. No other call_kind is valid; blocked calls create no receipt.

canonical_json_hash_protocol.canonical_full_file_rule: Exact full-file bytes must equal jq -cS compact lexicographic-key JSON plus exactly one LF; alternate whitespace, key order, escaping, or encoding fails even if parsing succeeds.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.classification_rule: Terminal/receipt payload hashes are immutable protocol-output hashes only, never a fifth GPE artifact.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.preparse_rejections: Reject duplicate object-member paths before parse, invalid UTF-8, any non-object or wrong top-level field set, and noncanonical bytes/encoding.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.receipt_payload: canonical full object with only receipt_sha256 removed; receipt_sha256 = SHA-256(canonical receipt_payload bytes). The displayed digest is serialized only after payload derivation and verifies canonical parsed payload, not final-file bytes.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.terminal_record_payload: canonical full object with only record_sha256 removed; record_sha256 = SHA-256(canonical terminal_record_payload bytes). The displayed digest is serialized only after payload derivation and verifies canonical parsed payload, not final-file bytes.

final_tree_record_protocol.common_guard: Every active descriptor first verifies the literal R20 generation and recorded digest. x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux require a lowercase-64-hex gpe-map-digest and reopen/re-hash all four GPE paths; aarch64-linux additionally validates explicit builder/emulation capability before action. Darwin derives the identical map only from matching successful x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux records. Every target recomputes the complete source snapshot, ignored inventory, coverage oracle, and exact base-key equality before reservation/action; missing, malformed, mismatch, or capability absence is zero action.
final_tree_record_protocol.descriptor_digest_rule: SHA-256 of canonical NUL-delimited target_descriptor_id, exact argv/guarded command, and expected output-map schema.
final_tree_record_protocol.descriptor_immutable_file_rule: For each of the three R20 descriptors, reservation is descriptor-scoped and terminal record, first receipt, and FV07 replay receipt are three distinct generation-specific files. Each is exclusive-created once and never appended or rewritten. The sole FV07 replay reads only its own terminal+first files and creates only its own replay receipt with zero target action; terminal failures are never replay-eligible and blocked calls create no receipt.
final_tree_record_protocol.descriptor_terminal_path_assertion: builder.terminal_path, aarch64_linux_builder.terminal_path, and cross_system.terminal_path byte-equal descriptor_immutable_file_paths.x86_64_linux.terminal, .aarch64_linux.terminal, and .aarch64_darwin.terminal respectively. Every first/FV07 replay receipt record_path byte-equals its own descriptor terminal path; record_sha256 verifies canonical parsed terminal_record_payload and canonical full-file bytes are separately enforced. No ambiguous linux/darwin key, R11 path, or extra descriptor record path is allowed.
final_tree_record_protocol.final_handoff_output_rule: For the active R20 session/source key, protocol-final-handoff at .agents/results/task-13-r20-final-verify-handoff-20260907.json must be absent before ANY FV01 dispatch. final-verify.sh exclusively creates it exactly once only after FV01–FV08 all accepted immutable outputs/verdicts/hashes. Preexisting, malformed, conflicting, or failed exclusive-create is a zero-dispatch hard blocker; never append, overwrite, reuse, or rebaseline. Final handoff contains no handoff_sha256 field; its external canonical full-file SHA-256 is the sole FV09 input. Its path is distinct from all FV01–FV08 output and all nine R20 descriptor immutable paths.
final_tree_record_protocol.final_verify_step_guard: Before and after each FV01–FV08 step, final-verify.sh calls this helper's snapshot verification rather than reimplementing it. Helper consumes only structured fv_input_sets[FVxx], expands repository_snapshot_selection=all, requires exact source_snapshot/input-set equality, and records canonical step_input_digest plus raw-result SHA; no inferred input is permitted.

fv01_observed_legacy_snapshot.canonical_schema: NUL-safe byte-sorted tuples: selected legacy path/kind/mode/content-SHA; seven exact document/span byte-SHAs; legacy HEAD; regular-file row count; NUL-safe status entries/fingerprint/count; recursive globs and exclusions
fv01_observed_legacy_snapshot.execution_rule: FV01 observes the selected legacy root before and after dispatch, requires observed-before==observed-after, compares both to the frozen literal expected selectors/fingerprint, and may PASS only on exact equality.

final_tree_record_protocol.fv07_rule: Before FV07 dispatch, fv_input_sets.FV07 binds the x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, and aarch64-darwin immutable terminal-record and first-receipt SHA values plus their identical recorded four-entry GPE map/map SHA for matching build_succeeded descriptors. FV07 dispatch is exactly linux-builder-check <r20-recorded-digest> <gpe-map-digest> fv07-replay, then aarch64-linux-builder-check <r20-recorded-digest> <gpe-map-digest> fv07-replay, then cross-system-verify <r20-recorded-digest> fv07-replay. These public adapters only validate recorded state, create one fixed current=0 replay receipt each, and perform no build/delegation. Wrong/generic/second replay blocks zero action. Handoff binds all three descriptor IDs/digests, terminal/first/replay hashes, assertion digest, snapshot, map, FV07 step digest, pre/post equality, and raw-result hash.

fv09_external_input_set.rule: FV09 consumes the final handoff externally; it has no FV01–FV08 step dispatch or shell execution.

final_tree_record_protocol.post_action_revalidation_rule: After every x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, or aarch64-darwin target action and before terminal success, helper reopens/re-hashes all four GPE paths into the exact canonical map, recomputes full repository source_snapshot, ignored inventory, generated-evidence binding, capability evidence where required, and descriptor input digest, then compares everything to the reservation/base key. Equality may commit build_succeeded with the exact output map. Any drift commits immutable input_drift with raw evidence and no success map; if action also fails, input_drift takes precedence.

prepare_snapshot_subcommand.failure_rule: Any preexisting, duplicate, conflicting, malformed, truncated, or partial GPE path; reservation conflict/interruption; failed exclusive create; staged/read-back byte mismatch including the fourth artifact; map-SHA mismatch; or prepublish/postpublish drift fails closed with no x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, or aarch64-darwin action, no overwrite/reuse/rebaseline, and a separately authorized new session. final_tree_record_protocol.terminal_rule: Holder terminalizes immutable build_succeeded/build_failed/input_drift record with canonical payload record_sha256 and exactly one call_kind=first receipt current=1. Only a build_succeeded descriptor permits exactly one later FV07-only zero-action replay, only with literal mode fv07-replay, which creates its fixed call_kind=fv07_replay receipt current=0. Terminal-present call without exact fv07-replay, wrong/generic mode, any second FV07 replay after that fixed receipt exists, or any later matching call is a zero-action hard block with a stable non-mutating error and no receipt/overwrite/reuse. Every build_failed/input_drift terminal failure blocks and is never replay-eligible or rerun. A sibling under same base_key plus target_descriptor_id with different descriptor_digest is hard conflict, never a new run.
final_tree_record_protocol.terminal_state_set_assertion: For all three R20 descriptor records terminal_state is exactly one of build_succeeded, build_failed, input_drift; missing, extra, or unknown values reject. build_succeeded alone has the target exact output map; build_failed requires failed action plus equal post-action inputs; input_drift preserves raw evidence/comparisons and has no success map. Any earlier descriptor failure blocks later matrix completion.

credential_value.algorithm: Set lowerLine = lib.toLower line, remove the first # comment suffix deterministically with builtins.split, then prepend one literal space to produce paddedContentLine. Fail when builtins.match regex paddedContentLine is non-null. The explicit preceding non-[a-z0-9_] boundary and required separator prevent larger-identifier matches; the required non-space/non-# value prevents empty/comment-only values.

executable_command.algorithm: fail when builtins.match regex line is non-null; builtins.match is whole-line, so the trailing .* is deliberate

non_loopback_url_or_host.algorithm: Set lowerLine = lib.toLower line. Use builtins.split url_candidate_split_regex lowerLine, retain only captured URL candidates deterministically, and split each candidate after the scheme at authority_split_regex; every authority must whole-match allowed_authority_regex. A line with one allowed and one forbidden URL fails. Separately use builtins.split bare_candidate_split_regex lowerLine, filter empty fragments, retain tokens whole-matching bare_candidate_regex or bare_ipv6_regex, and reject every retained token except allowed_bare_candidates. Bracketed IPv6 literals and unbracketed concrete IPv6 addresses containing at least two colons are recognized; only ::1 and [::1] are allowed, with a decimal port allowed only in bracketed authority or endpoint syntax. Ordinary undotted prose is never a candidate, Markdown punctuation is a split delimiter, and objectStorage.createLocally is accepted only by its exact lowercased token.

nonempty_assignment.algorithm: fail when builtins.match regex line is non-null; whole-line match is explicit

pem.algorithm: fail when builtins.match regex line is non-null; whole-line match is explicit

positive_host_guidance.algorithm: Set lowerLine = lib.toLower line, split with token_split_regex, and filter empty tokens deterministically. Fail when any whole action token occurs before a later whole host token. hostname and reversed host/action order do not match. The byte-exact sigv4-host normative statement is the sole allowed matching line.

production_absolute_path.algorithm: Prepend one literal space to produce paddedLine, then fail when builtins.match regex paddedLine is non-null; whole-line match and its explicit preceding space-or-code-delimiter boundary are deliberate

deployment_boundary.fixture_evidence: deployment-boundary names every listed fixture result internally; the canonical positive contains all six exact manifest marker/statement pairs, loopback URLs with and without decimal ports/paths, bracketed and unbracketed loopback IPv6 forms, objectStorage.createLocally, harmless larger credential/Host identifiers, and the byte-exact SigV4 exception. Nested fixture results never add top-level PASS/FAIL/SKIP entries.
deployment_boundary.marker_rule: Each literal marker `<!-- task13:<id> -->` occurs exactly once and is immediately followed by its exact normative statement on the next line.
deployment_boundary.matching_semantics: All predicates are implementable in tests/nix/module-eval.nix without a helper: builtins.match is whole-string POSIX ERE matching only; no PCRE-only lookaround, backreference, inline flag, or word/digit/whitespace shorthand escape is permitted. For case-insensitive checks compute lowerLine = lib.toLower line first. Token boundaries are explicit ASCII classes or deterministic builtins.split token lists with empty/capture fragments removed.
deployment_boundary.positive_host_exception: The byte-exact sigv4-host normative statement above is the only allowed action-before-host line. Mentioning Podman in required local-development prose is allowed, but shell command guidance is not.
required_markers: local-podman-compose
Rootless Podman Compose is local-development-only and MUST NOT be used for production deployment.
native-nixos-systemd
Native NixOS systemd is the sole production deployment path for this repository.
native-minio
Optional native MinIO co-deployment is controlled only by objectStorage.createLocally.
migration-policy
Migrations default to manual; api-prestart is the only optional automated mode.
homelab-ownership
Homelab owns PostgreSQL, Redis, Podman, host, domain, volumes, ingress, secrets, monitoring, backup, and restore.
sigv4-host
MUST NOT unconditionally set, rewrite, or override the MinIO/S3 Host header; SigV4 requires preserving the caller's signed Host value.

env_timing_boundary.authoritative_timing_precedence: All nine non-secret timing module options are authoritative for both api and worker. Each exposes exactly `serviceConfig.EnvironmentFile = [ opaqueEnvironmentFile generatedTimingEnvironmentFile ]`: opaque user/SOPS environmentFile first; Task-13-generated non-secret timing file second, so the generated file wins under systemd.exec EnvironmentFile semantics (later file wins; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/main/man/systemd.exec.xml lines 2963-2965). The opaque file must not own these keys; any external duplicate is overridden and is never opened, read, or logged by module-eval tests. generatedTimingEnvironmentFile is the sole timing-value producer and direct serviceConfig.Environment contains none of the nine keys for either service.
env_timing_boundary.line_rule: Each listed key occurs exactly once and its whole line matches `^KEY=[1-9][0-9]*$`, substituting KEY literally; all pre-existing keys outside this list are ignored and environmentFile is never opened.

service_timing_environmentfile_mappings.direct_environment_rule: Neither api nor worker serviceConfig.Environment contains any of the nine timing keys.
service_timing_environmentfile_mappings.generated_file_rule: generatedTimingEnvironmentFile is second and contains every timing key exactly once; it is the sole timing-value producer.
service_timing_environmentfile_mappings.opaque_duplicate_rule: Module-eval proves opaque duplicate values are overridden without opening, reading, or logging opaque content.
service_timing_environmentfile_mappings.rule: timing-invariant-module proves the shared api/worker ordered EnvironmentFile list, generated second-file exact-nine-key sole-production rule, opaque-duplicate override without opaque inspection, direct-Environment absence of all nine keys, and each resolved triplet inequality; env-timing-boundary is supplemental only.

final_tree_record_protocol.atomic_reservation_rule: Before delegation/build, helper uses descriptor-keyed same-filesystem mkdir as the sole portable exclusive primitive. It provides process/concurrency/interruption-safe atomic reservation only; no fsync, directory durability, crash/power-loss persistence, atomic-rename durability, or capability preflight is claimed. Only the mkdir holder may invoke once. Concurrent loser or an existing reservation directory after interruption is a zero-action hard blocker; no TTL, reclaim, delete, overwrite, or automatic retry.
final_tree_record_protocol.call_kind_rule: Only exact JSON token call_kind=first is valid for the initial receipt, and only exact JSON token call_kind=fv07_replay is valid for the sole FV07 replay receipt. No other call_kind is valid; blocked calls create no receipt.

canonical_json_hash_protocol.canonical_full_file_rule: Exact full-file bytes must equal jq -cS compact lexicographic-key JSON plus exactly one LF; alternate whitespace, key order, escaping, or encoding fails even if parsing succeeds.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.classification_rule: Terminal/receipt payload hashes are immutable protocol-output hashes only, never a fifth GPE artifact.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.preparse_rejections: Reject duplicate object-member paths before parse, invalid UTF-8, any non-object or wrong top-level field set, and noncanonical bytes/encoding.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.receipt_payload: canonical full object with only receipt_sha256 removed; receipt_sha256 = SHA-256(canonical receipt_payload bytes). The displayed digest is serialized only after payload derivation and verifies canonical parsed payload, not final-file bytes.
canonical_json_hash_protocol.terminal_record_payload: canonical full object with only record_sha256 removed; record_sha256 = SHA-256(canonical terminal_record_payload bytes). The displayed digest is serialized only after payload derivation and verifies canonical parsed payload, not final-file bytes.

final_tree_record_protocol.common_guard: Every active descriptor first verifies the literal R21 generation and recorded digest. x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux require a lowercase-64-hex gpe-map-digest and reopen/re-hash all four GPE paths; aarch64-linux additionally validates explicit builder/emulation capability before action. Darwin derives the identical map only from matching successful x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux records. Every target recomputes the complete source snapshot, ignored inventory, coverage oracle, and exact base-key equality before reservation/action; missing, malformed, mismatch, or capability absence is zero action.
final_tree_record_protocol.descriptor_digest_rule: SHA-256 of canonical NUL-delimited target_descriptor_id, exact argv/guarded command, and expected output-map schema.
final_tree_record_protocol.descriptor_immutable_file_rule: For each of the three R21 descriptors, reservation is descriptor-scoped and terminal record, first receipt, and FV07 replay receipt are three distinct generation-specific files. Each is exclusive-created once and never appended or rewritten. The sole FV07 replay reads only its own terminal+first files and creates only its own replay receipt with zero target action; terminal failures are never replay-eligible and blocked calls create no receipt.
final_tree_record_protocol.descriptor_terminal_path_assertion: builder.terminal_path, aarch64_linux_builder.terminal_path, and cross_system.terminal_path byte-equal descriptor_immutable_file_paths.x86_64_linux.terminal, .aarch64_linux.terminal, and .aarch64_darwin.terminal respectively. Every first/FV07 replay receipt record_path byte-equals its own descriptor terminal path; record_sha256 verifies canonical parsed terminal_record_payload and canonical full-file bytes are separately enforced. No ambiguous linux/darwin key, R11 path, or extra descriptor record path is allowed.
final_tree_record_protocol.final_handoff_output_rule: For the active R21 session/source key, protocol-final-handoff at .agents/results/task-13-r21-final-verify-handoff-20260907.json must be absent before ANY FV01 dispatch. scripts/tasks/task-13/final-verify-r21.sh, invoked only as an internal frozen helper after the strict top-level final-verify-r21-exec card, exclusively creates it exactly once only after FV01-FV08 all accepted immutable outputs, verdicts, and hashes. The helper is never an operator entrypoint. Preexisting, malformed, conflicting, or failed exclusive-create is a zero-dispatch hard blocker; never append, overwrite, reuse, or rebaseline. Final handoff contains no handoff_sha256 field; its external canonical full-file SHA-256 is the sole FV09 input. Its path is distinct from all FV01-FV08 output and all nine R21 descriptor immutable paths.
final_tree_record_protocol.final_verify_step_guard: Before and after each FV01-FV08 step, scripts/tasks/task-13/final-verify-r21.sh internally calls scripts/tasks/task-13/final-tree-record-r21.sh snapshot verification after the strict top-level final-verify-r21-exec card; neither frozen helper is an operator entrypoint. The record helper consumes only structured fv_input_sets[FVxx], expands repository_snapshot_selection=all, requires exact source_snapshot/input-set equality, and records canonical step_input_digest plus raw-result SHA; no inferred input is permitted.

fv_output_sets.rule: For the session/source key each listed path must be absent before its producer dispatch and exclusive-created once after dispatch as immutable protocol output; preexisting, malformed, or conflicting output is a zero-action hard blocker with no stale reuse/overwrite. input_coverage_oracle.rule: Machine-checkable base union requires every repository or explicit ignored/external mutable input exactly once in one classification/subkind; missing, extra, duplicate, self-referential, unclassified, or unconsumed input fails before any action. The closed subkind set is exact and unique; unknown/missing/extra subkind fails. Repository snapshot uses all tracked plus untracked-nonignored paths; ignored evidence requires inventory SHA-256. The tracked catalog separately declares exactly four generated_protocol_evidence descriptors; after base oracle completion helper binds their three prior component hashes and later source-hash artifact link without content self-inventory. Other protocol output requires explicit hash linkage.

final_tree_record_protocol.new_source_rule: A changed source snapshot, ignored-evidence inventory, or any byte/hash/map entry of the four GPE paths requires separately authorized verification/session; helper never relocks, rebaselines, silently recomputes a replacement, or overwrites a reservation/terminal record.
final_tree_record_protocol.post_action_revalidation_rule: After every x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, or aarch64-darwin target action and before terminal success, helper reopens/re-hashes all four GPE paths into the exact canonical map, recomputes full repository source_snapshot, ignored inventory, generated-evidence binding, capability evidence where required, and descriptor input digest, then compares everything to the reservation/base key. Equality may commit build_succeeded with the exact output map. Any drift commits immutable input_drift with raw evidence and no success map; if action also fails, input_drift takes precedence.

prepare_snapshot_subcommand.failure_rule: Any preexisting, duplicate, conflicting, malformed, truncated, or partial GPE path; reservation conflict/interruption; failed exclusive create; staged/read-back byte mismatch including the fourth artifact; map-SHA mismatch; or prepublish/postpublish drift fails closed with no x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, or aarch64-darwin action, no overwrite/reuse/rebaseline, and a separately authorized new session. final_tree_record_protocol.sole_implementation_owner: This helper alone materializes/validates the complete final source snapshot and ignored-evidence inventory, resolves all three R21 descriptor-scoped keys, acquires portable atomic reservations, terminalizes/hashes immutable records, rejects stale/malformed/duplicate/nonterminal/conflicting state, and emits one first receipt plus the sole FV07 replay receipt for each public target descriptor. final_tree_record_protocol.step_input_digest_rule: SHA-256 of canonical NUL-delimited FV ID, full expanded repository component hash/ordered repo:<relative-path> ID array, concrete ordered explicit ignored/external input IDs/hashes, the exact recorded four-entry gpe_artifact_hash_map plus gpe_artifact_hash_map_sha256, canonical dispatch descriptor, and preexisting immutable protocol-output IDs/hashes. final_tree_record_protocol.terminal_rule: Holder terminalizes immutable build_succeeded/build_failed/input_drift record with canonical payload record_sha256 and exactly one call_kind=first receipt current=1. Only a build_succeeded descriptor permits exactly one later FV07-only zero-action replay, only with literal mode fv07-replay, which creates its fixed call_kind=fv07_replay receipt current=0. Terminal-present call without exact fv07-replay, wrong/generic mode, any second FV07 replay after that fixed receipt exists, or any later matching call is a zero-action hard block with a stable non-mutating error and no receipt/overwrite/reuse. Every build_failed/input_drift terminal failure blocks and is never replay-eligible or rerun. A sibling under same base_key plus target_descriptor_id with different descriptor_digest is hard conflict, never a new run.
final_tree_record_protocol.terminal_state_set_assertion: For all three R21 descriptor records terminal_state is exactly one of build_succeeded, build_failed, input_drift; missing, extra, or unknown values reject. build_succeeded alone has the target exact output map; build_failed requires failed action plus equal post-action inputs; input_drift preserves raw evidence/comparisons and has no success map. Any earlier descriptor failure blocks later matrix completion.

final_tree_snapshot.catalog_completion_rule: catalog_required_entries must byte-for-byte equal, in canonical order, catalog_fixed_entries IDs followed by the four generated_protocol_evidence IDs followed by every catalog_protocol_output_entries ID; duplicate, missing, or extra ID fails. rejected_alternatives.alternative: Decompose Task-13 into a single non-sequential sprint covering package/module/coverage/docs together.
rejected_alternatives.rejected_reason: This produces an unreviewable RED/GREEN batch and obscures which of the eleven locked acceptance-criteria groups (output families, package matrix, test/coverage separation, task-owned commands, module systemd wiring, MinIO branches, homelab boundary, secret hygiene, lease/timeout controls, contract-drift reuse, documentation) is satisfied by which evidence. Rejected in favor of five sequential sprints (t13-s1..t13-s5), each with a distinct evidence responsibility and RED only where a meaningful behavioral distinction exists before implementation.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Verify the NixOS module with a full `nixos-test` VM boot test that actually starts systemd, MinIO, and the api/worker services.
rejected_alternatives.rejected_reason: VM tests require Linux/KVM, unavailable from the aarch64-darwin development machine and not guaranteed reproducible on a remote Linux builder without an additional unpinned hypervisor dependency. The locked acceptance criteria use one x86_64-linux nixosSystem dry fixture for rendered Linux systemd/option behavior and pure external lib.evalModules provenance fixtures for both supported systems, not live service behavior. Rejected in favor of static module evaluation in t13-s4, deferring any future live-service proof to homelab's own deployment validation, which is explicitly out of this repository's scope.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Use cargo-tarpaulin for the line-coverage gate.
rejected_alternatives.rejected_reason: Tarpaulin's ptrace-based instrumentation is Linux-only and unreliable in sandboxed/Nix build environments, and does not support the aarch64-darwin development system the coverage recipe must also run on locally. Rejected in favor of cargo-llvm-cov, which uses LLVM source-based coverage compatible with the existing fenix/rustc toolchain on both supported systems and integrates with a `--fail-under-lines` threshold flag without a second instrumentation pass.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Hand-roll a bespoke systemd unit and imperative script for local MinIO instead of configuring upstream NixOS `services.minio`.
rejected_alternatives.rejected_reason: A hand-rolled unit duplicates user/group/dataDir/service lifecycle logic nixpkgs already implements and maintains upstream, increasing Task-13's own review and reproducibility surface without new capability. Rejected in favor of directly configuring services.minio and limiting nix/module.nix to only the loopback-console, rootCredentialsFile, and non-blocking after/wants wiring genuinely required by the locked criteria.

The static assertion script obtains only sorted top-level output names without forcing or JSON-serializing function-valued outputs (for example, `nix eval --json path:.# --apply builtins.attrNames`), and requires the exact set `checks,devShells,nixosModules,packages`. Every missing or extra top-level family is a deterministic named `top-level flake output key-set mismatch` failure; the current missing `nixosModules` is one baseline failure. It separately probes required devShells/packages/checks family shapes per supported system via `nix eval --json` / `nix flake show --json`, never a bare tool crash.

The same non-forcing shape probe freezes `expectedSystems` as the sorted set `aarch64-darwin,x86_64-linux` and independently compares sorted `builtins.attrNames outputs.packages`, `builtins.attrNames outputs.devShells`, and `builtins.attrNames outputs.checks` against it before inspecting children. Its stable assertion name is `per-system output family system key-sets exact`; nested evidence names `packages`, `devShells`, and `checks` with each observed key set. A missing or extra system fails this assertion with the affected family and differing key named. The current scaffold must PASS this assertion, so it never becomes a fourth baseline RED failure; the probe neither forces a child derivation nor evaluates or serializes `nixosModules.default`.

The `nixosModules` child key set is checked only after the top-level parent exists, using a non-forcing, JSON-serializable child-name/presence probe (for example `nix eval --json path:.#nixosModules --apply builtins.attrNames`, sorted, plus `nix eval --json path:.#nixosModules --apply 'modules: modules ? default'`). It requires exactly the singleton `default` and never evaluates or serializes `nixosModules.default`, because an actual NixOS module is a function and is not JSON-serializable. While the parent is absent in baseline RED, report `nixosModules child key-set exact (default only): blocked/skipped: nixosModules parent absent`, not a failure. This shape probe proves only parent/child keys; actual module option/config behavior remains reserved for t13-s4's `nixosSystem`/`evalModules` assertions.

The script additionally asserts, per supported system, that `packages.<system>`'s sorted key set is exactly `api,worker` (e.g. via `nix eval --json path:.#packages.<system> --apply builtins.attrNames`, sorted and joined) and reports any extra key — including the currently-present `default` — as a distinct named failure (`packages.<system> key-set mismatch (extra default)`), never merely a presence check on api/worker alone.

The script also asserts, per supported system, that `devShells.<system>`'s sorted key set is exactly the singleton `default` (e.g. via `nix eval --json path:.#devShells.<system> --apply builtins.attrNames`, sorted and joined) and reports this as a distinct named assertion (`devShells.<system> key-set exact (default only)`); this assertion is expected to PASS against the current unverified scaffold (no extra devShell key exists today) and is not one of the three currently-failing assertions.

The script asserts, without forcing check derivations, that every `checks.<system>` sorted child-name set is exactly `api,architecture,cargo-clippy,cargo-fmt,cargo-test-all-features,cargo-test-default,contract-drift,worker`. It reports a missing or extra child only as `checks.<system> key-set mismatch (...)`; against the current scaffold the sole check-related RED failure is `checks.<system> key-set mismatch (missing contract-drift)`. `checks.contract-drift absent` is retired and must never be emitted as a duplicate failure.

The script confirms `per-system output family system key-sets exact` PASSes for packages/devShells/checks with the exact two expected system keys, then confirms the devShells/checks family child assertions for both systems (existing flake.nix), including `devShells.<system> key-set exact (default only)` passing. The top-level exact-output assertion fails because `nixosModules` is missing, the packages child key-set assertion fails due to the extra `default` key, and the exact checks child key-set assertion fails only because contract-drift is missing. It reports exactly those three named failures (`top-level flake output key-set mismatch (missing nixosModules)`, `packages.<system> key-set mismatch (extra default)`, `checks.<system> key-set mismatch (missing contract-drift)`); the nested nixosModules child-key assertion is explicitly blocked/skipped by the missing parent and is never a second failure.

The script asserts flake.nix's `supportedSystems` list is exactly `["aarch64-darwin" "x86_64-linux"]` in that order, and that no second Rust channel/profile/component/target declaration exists outside the single documented `fenix.fromToolchainFile` call referencing rust-toolchain.toml.
